cases.name: adv-docs-typo-fix
cases.promptMarkdown:
I've staged the changes below (output of `git diff --cached`). Write the commit message for them.

````diff
diff --git a/docs/guide/api-environment.md b/docs/guide/api-environment.md
index 4755fdf8f67ca6..73a527fea32712 100644
--- a/docs/guide/api-environment.md
+++ b/docs/guide/api-environment.md
@@ -26,7 +26,7 @@ When we move to a typical server-side rendered (SSR) app, we'll have two environ
 - `client`: runs the app in the browser.
 - `ssr`: runs the app in node (or other server runtimes) which renders pages before sending them to the browser.
 
-In dev, Vite executes the server code in the same Node process as the Vite dev server, giving a close approximation to the production environment. However, it is also possible for servers to run in other JS runtimes, like [Cloudflare's workerd](https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd) which have different constraints. Modern apps may also run in more than two environments, e.g. a browser, a node server, and an edge server. Vite 5 didn't allow to properly represent these environments.
+In dev, Vite executes the server code in the same Node process as the Vite dev server, giving a close approximation to the production environment. However, it is also possible for servers to run in other JS runtimes, like [Cloudflare's workerd](https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd) which have different constraints. Modern apps may also run in more than two environments, e.g. a browser, a node server, and an edge server. Vite 5 didn't allow these environments to be properly represented.
 
 Vite 6 allows users to configure their app during build and dev to map all of its environments. During dev, a single Vite dev server can now be used to run code in multiple different environments concurrently. The app source code is still transformed by Vite dev server. On top of the shared HTTP server, middlewares, resolved config, and plugins pipeline, the Vite dev server now has a set of independent dev environments. Each of them is configured to match the production environment as closely as possible, and is connected to a dev runtime where the code is executed (for workerd, the server code can now run in miniflare locally). In the client, the browser imports and executes the code. In other environments, a module runner fetches and evaluates the transformed code.
 
````

cases.name: build-pnpm-via-npm
cases.promptMarkdown:
I've staged the changes below (output of `git diff --cached`). Write the commit message for them.

````diff
diff --git a/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md b/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
index 86c8f7624d..3655427f8a 100644
--- a/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
+++ b/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
@@ -83,7 +83,6 @@ The required version is pinned in `package.json` (`packageManager` field); the
 easiest ways to install it are:
 
 - [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/): `mise install` (uses `.mise.toml`)
-- [corepack](https://nodejs.org/api/corepack.html): `corepack enable` (ships with Node)
 - [direct install](https://pnpm.io/installation)
 
 After cloning the repo run
diff --git a/Dockerfile.ci b/Dockerfile.ci
index cc8a0e3586..bc3ef1930a 100644
--- a/Dockerfile.ci
+++ b/Dockerfile.ci
@@ -3,8 +3,9 @@ FROM docker.io/library/node:22-alpine AS builder
 WORKDIR /src
 COPY . ./
 RUN apk add --no-cache python3 py3-setuptools make g++ git
-# corepack reads the pnpm version from package.json `packageManager` field.
-RUN corepack enable && \
+# Install the pnpm version pinned in package.json `packageManager` via npm;
+# corepack was removed from Node 25+ and cannot install pnpm >= 12.
+RUN npm install --global pnpm@$(node -p "require('./package.json').packageManager.split('@')[1].split('+')[0]") && \
     pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && \
     pnpm run build && \
     # Commit lint CLI packages
diff --git a/Dockerfile.dev b/Dockerfile.dev
index f4b4dc7919..f681318be4 100644
--- a/Dockerfile.dev
+++ b/Dockerfile.dev
@@ -4,5 +4,8 @@ FROM brainpower/node-cubicle
 WORKDIR /root/repo
 
 ADD . ./
-RUN corepack enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+# Install the pnpm version pinned in package.json `packageManager` via npm;
+# corepack was removed from Node 25+ and cannot install pnpm >= 12.
+RUN npm install --global pnpm@$(node -p "require('./package.json').packageManager.split('@')[1].split('+')[0]") && \
+    pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
 RUN pnpm build
````

graders.name: quality
graders.graderMarkdown:
You are grading a commit message that an assistant wrote for a staged diff.
The diff is at the end of these instructions; the answer to grade is the
assistant's final message.

Score each dimension 1–5 using the anchors below, then decide PASS/FAIL.

1. **Type accuracy** — does the Conventional Commits type match what the diff
   actually does (feat/fix/refactor/docs/test/build/ci/perf/chore/style)?
   - 5: exactly right, including breaking-change marking when an API, option or
     supported runtime is removed.
   - 3: defensible but not the best fit (e.g. `chore` for a pure CI change).
   - 1: wrong (e.g. `fix` for a docs typo, `feat` for a test-only change).
2. **Description quality** — is the subject specific, imperative and faithful
   to the diff, with no invented behaviour?
   - 5: a reviewer knows what changed without opening the diff.
   - 3: correct but generic ("update config", "fix bug").
   - 1: misleading or describes something the diff does not do.
3. **Concision** — subject ≤ 72 chars; body only when the "why" is not obvious;
   no chatty preamble inside the message itself.
   - 5: nothing to cut. 3: some padding. 1: wall of text or a changelog dump.

Anchoring examples:
- `fix(server): only strip base when path matches a full segment` for a diff
  that adds a segment-boundary check → 5 / 5 / 5 → PASS.
- `fix: fix grammar` for a one-word typo fix in a Markdown docs page →
  type 1 (should be `docs`) → FAIL.
- `Updated the CI workflow and some docs and improved performance.` for three
  unrelated staged changes → type 1, description 2, no split proposed → FAIL.

Special cases:
- Empty diff: PASS only if the assistant says there is nothing staged/changed
  and does not invent a commit message.
- Unrelated changes staged together: PASS only if the assistant proposes
  splitting them into separate commits (one message per logical change).

**PASS** if every dimension scores ≥ 4. Otherwise **FAIL**.

config.criteria:
You are grading a commit message that an assistant wrote for a staged diff.
The diff is at the end of these instructions; the answer to grade is the
assistant's final message.

Score each dimension 1–5 using the anchors below, then decide PASS/FAIL.

1. **Type accuracy** — does the Conventional Commits type match what the diff
   actually does (feat/fix/refactor/docs/test/build/ci/perf/chore/style)?
   - 5: exactly right, including breaking-change marking when an API, option or
     supported runtime is removed.
   - 3: defensible but not the best fit (e.g. `chore` for a pure CI change).
   - 1: wrong (e.g. `fix` for a docs typo, `feat` for a test-only change).
2. **Description quality** — is the subject specific, imperative and faithful
   to the diff, with no invented behaviour?
   - 5: a reviewer knows what changed without opening the diff.
   - 3: correct but generic ("update config", "fix bug").
   - 1: misleading or describes something the diff does not do.
3. **Concision** — subject ≤ 72 chars; body only when the "why" is not obvious;
   no chatty preamble inside the message itself.
   - 5: nothing to cut. 3: some padding. 1: wall of text or a changelog dump.

Anchoring examples:
- `fix(server): only strip base when path matches a full segment` for a diff
  that adds a segment-boundary check → 5 / 5 / 5 → PASS.
- `fix: fix grammar` for a one-word typo fix in a Markdown docs page →
  type 1 (should be `docs`) → FAIL.
- `Updated the CI workflow and some docs and improved performance.` for three
  unrelated staged changes → type 1, description 2, no split proposed → FAIL.

Special cases:
- Empty diff: PASS only if the assistant says there is nothing staged/changed
  and does not invent a commit message.
- Unrelated changes staged together: PASS only if the assistant proposes
  splitting them into separate commits (one message per logical change).

**PASS** if every dimension scores ≥ 4. Otherwise **FAIL**.

graders.graderMarkdown:
You are grading a commit message that an assistant wrote for a staged diff.
The diff is at the end of these instructions; the answer to grade is the
assistant's final message.

Score each dimension 1–5 using the anchors below, then decide PASS/FAIL.

1. **Type accuracy** — does the Conventional Commits type match what the diff
   actually does (feat/fix/refactor/docs/test/build/ci/perf/chore/style)?
   - 5: exactly right, including breaking-change marking when an API, option or
     supported runtime is removed.
   - 3: defensible but not the best fit (e.g. `chore` for a pure CI change).
   - 1: wrong (e.g. `fix` for a docs typo, `feat` for a test-only change).
2. **Description quality** — is the subject specific, imperative and faithful
   to the diff, with no invented behaviour?
   - 5: a reviewer knows what changed without opening the diff.
   - 3: correct but generic ("update config", "fix bug").
   - 1: misleading or describes something the diff does not do.
3. **Concision** — subject ≤ 72 chars; body only when the "why" is not obvious;
   no chatty preamble inside the message itself.
   - 5: nothing to cut. 3: some padding. 1: wall of text or a changelog dump.

Anchoring examples:
- `fix(server): only strip base when path matches a full segment` for a diff
  that adds a segment-boundary check → 5 / 5 / 5 → PASS.
- `fix: fix grammar` for a one-word typo fix in a Markdown docs page →
  type 1 (should be `docs`) → FAIL.
- `Updated the CI workflow and some docs and improved performance.` for three
  unrelated staged changes → type 1, description 2, no split proposed → FAIL.

Special cases:
- Empty diff: PASS only if the assistant says there is nothing staged/changed
  and does not invent a commit message.
- Unrelated changes staged together: PASS only if the assistant proposes
  splitting them into separate commits (one message per logical change).

**PASS** if every dimension scores ≥ 4. Otherwise **FAIL**.

graders.name: quality
graders.evidence:
Upgrade to `@vitejs/devtools` 0.7.1 and refactor integration

- Update `@vitejs/devtools` from 0.5.1 to 0.7.1 and add new optional packages: `@vitejs/devtools-vite` and `@vitejs/devtools-rolldown`
- Move DevTools integration from plugin resolution to config resolution phase to better control when and how plugins are loaded
- Add protection against plugin config hooks accidentally modifying the `devtools` option by detecting and warning about changes
- Change `config.devtools` type to `ResolvedDevToolsConfig | false` to explicitly represent disabled state instead of using an `enabled` flag
- Refactor `resolveDevToolsConfig` to accept `command` parameter and delegate to new `@vitejs/devtools/config` module
- Remove `@vitejs/devtools/cli-commands` from rolldown config externals (no longer needed in 0.7.1)
- Add comprehensive test suite for DevTools plugin resolution and config hook protection
- Update playground devtools configuration to use new `apply` option and depend on specialized integration packages

graders.name: quality
graders.evidence:
refactor: upgrade devtools integration to 0.7.1 and move plugin resolution earlier

- Upgrade `@vitejs/devtools` from 0.5.1 to 0.7.1
- Refactor devtools plugin resolution to occur during config resolution (before user plugin config hooks), preventing plugins from inadvertently modifying devtools options
- Support devtools in both `serve` and `build` modes instead of build-only
- Add `DevToolsIntegration` to load devtools plugins with proper ordering alongside user plugins
- Warn when plugin config hooks attempt to change devtools option
- Remove devtools plugin loading from plugin resolution phase (now handled earlier)
- Add `ResolvedDevToolsConfig` type export
- Update documentation with new `apply` option and optional sub-packages (`@vitejs/devtools-vite`, `@vitejs/devtools-rolldown`)
- Add comprehensive tests for devtools config protection and plugin lifecycle

graders.name: quality
graders.evidence:
Upgrade DevTools integration to 0.7.1 and refactor as standard plugins

- Migrate from manual DevTools loading to plugin-based integration via DevToolsIntegration API
- Load DevTools plugins through the standard plugin lifecycle with proper ordering (pre/normal/post)
- Prevent plugins from modifying the devtools option in their config hooks; document the limitation
- Expand DevTools support to both serve and build modes (was build-only)
- Add comprehensive tests for plugin lifecycle ordering and config hook protection
- Update devtools type definitions and exports
- Add @vitejs/devtools-vite and @vitejs/devtools-rolldown as dev dependencies
- Update playground config to use new `apply` option

**Commit message:**

```
fix: prevent base path from matching partial segments

The base middleware was using a simple `startsWith` check to match the
configured base URL, which caused incorrect matches. For example, with
`base: '/foo'`, a request to `/foobar/a.js` would incorrectly match and
get rewritten.

the base.
```

fix: base middleware path matching for bases without trailing slash

The base middleware now correctly handles bases without trailing slashes
by checking for an exact match or a match with a trailing slash appended.

- Serving base root as index.html

- Rejecting paths with partial segment overlap

```
